tools.description:
Report the resolved configuration: build, roots, allowed repos, provider keys left
unused, and, on a role-launched server, the tool server name and agent binding.
Read-only; reflects the settings and runtime loaded at startup. Longer explanation:
docs/tool-details.md.

tools.description: Orient a repository or leaf; leaf calls pass task_context. include_drift measures the reference anchors of onboarding cards and validity of the tree; omit it and nothing is measured. Staleness never blocks by itself. Currentness: knowledge_read and knowledge_integrity_check. MIK-R30: update the card or record why not; citation_fix repairs moved anchors, a curator re-authors stale ones. Nothing is repaired here. include_freshness fetches remotes and writes FETCH_HEAD. More: docs/tool-details.md.

tools.description:
Name which knowledge governs up to 20 paths (MIK-R109).

Per path: existence, its governing card with `cardStatus`, record counts, and the
action-asking records by ID, kind, state and heading. `openWeaknesses` and
`dependentDocuments` are one count each, absent at zero. No text is returned: open the
files yourself. `refresh` is removed. Leaf calls pass `task_context`; `worktreeScope`,
`sourceRoot` and `memoryRoot` name both. Longer explanation: docs/reference/mcp-tools.md.

tools.description:
Install or refresh the packaged coordinator runtime into the coordination root, safe
to re-run. Preserves user data (memory-repos/, providers/data/); replaces the scaffold
(skills/, docs/) and prunes legacy binaries. No provider install/start/watch
path remains: the install stops leftover watchers and reports enabled provider keys
once as unused. The final host part provisions the build-pinned host/plugin from the
shared paseoRuntime block; it never writes shared settings and defers needed restarts.
Preview first with dry_run=true: it changes nothing. Longer explanation:
docs/tool-details.md.
tools.name: runtime_install

tools.description: Retire one authorized direct child seat using task_document_ref, role and reason. Only its starter may retire it; interrupt_turn is required for a running turn. Repeats are inert. More: docs/tool-details.md.

tools.description:
Check memory before closeout: findings, counts and the checklist location, not semantic
certification. Pass a sync, start or poll request; candidate runs use the leaf contract.
Ready memory also requires validated curator_coherence. Four operations have no tool, by
design: the conversion (it runs inside the crossing sync, or once per repository), the
index build (every read builds it on demand), the formatter (the writer renders canonical
files), and the worklist (this tool computes it and `knowledge_integrity_check` returns
it). Longer explanation: docs/tool-details.md.

tools.description: Repair moved citation anchors in a leaf memory worktree. Pass repo_id and contract_path, with documents for a batch or document for one card; preview with dry_run. Renames, deletions and ambiguous anchors remain curator work. Old-format memory is refused: convert before repair. Converted repairs author sidecar references; full lists are in logged detail. Longer explanation: docs/tool-details.md.
tools.name: citation_fix

tools.description: Refresh route indexes for a leaf memory worktree using repo_id and contract_path. Preview with dry_run; unscoped writes require pre-baseline admission. More: docs/tool-details.md.
tools.name: route_index_refresh

tools.description:
Initialize or repair a repository's memory root (scaffold `system/` files, the
`onboarding/` and `docs/` layout, optionally `git init`). `initial_branch` names the code
branch the memory is the foundation of: it becomes the memory repository's initial branch
and the recorded `agents-remember.defaultBranch` that baseline adoption and every worktree
entry point check against. Omitted, it defaults to the configured code repository's
currently checked-out branch, and the call refuses rather than inventing a name when
neither is available. Creates missing paths only and never overwrites existing onboarding
content. Preview with dry_run=true. Usually driven by the c-00-initialize-memory-repo
skill.
tools.name: memory_init

tools.description:
Report drift and Git attribution state to decide whether an external-memory baseline can be
adopted. Read-only.
tools.name: memory_baseline_status

tools.description: Adopt the first attributed external-memory baseline and commit memory. Pass repo_id; preview with dry_run. accept_drift permits stale anchors, never validator violations. More: docs/tool-details.md.
tools.name: memory_baseline_adopt

tools.description: Plan converted pairs/records at equal versions; observe official-code anchors, review conflicts. Curator authors history; no commit/report. More: docs/tool-details.md.
tools.name: memory_carryover_plan

tools.description: Apply converted pairs/records; reanchor, index, validate. Refusal restores bytes; skip edited targets, retry safely. No commit/history carry; curator authors rows before closeout. Requires intent_note. More: docs/tool-details.md.
tools.name: memory_carryover_apply

tools.description:
Create or load a task contract with its code and memory worktrees.

Answers the state reached (started, would-start, blocked) and the next call with its
arguments; the whole result is in the log file. Poll worktree_status for progress. A
dry run changes no task document, no contract, no Git ref and no worktree, and the
call is recorded in the observer log like every tool call. It does not read the
dependencies a packet names: leaves start in parallel and are synchronised later, so
the order of landing is the manager's decision. Reference:
docs/reference/mcp-tools.md.
tools.name: worktree_start

tools.description:
Explicitly adopt one readable pre-locator enclosure. Dry-run by default. This is the
only old-layout address migration. It validates one exact contract/root, preserves
source digests and an audit receipt, and never runs from normal status, control,
contract writes, or schema-1 repair. Answers the state reached. Reference:
docs/reference/mcp-tools.md.
tools.name: worktree_enclosure_adopt

tools.description:
Re-attach to an existing task contract without mutating Git. Answers the state reached
(attached, attached-existing-contract, blocked) and the next call; the whole result is
in the log file. Reference: docs/reference/mcp-tools.md.
tools.name: worktree_attach

tools.description:
Report a task worktree's lifecycle status: the phase reached (worktree-started,
integration-pending, closeout-pending, integration-blocked, carryover-pending,
cleanup-pending, cleanup-completed, abandoned), what blocks, the one
following call, and whether task-document copies differ from their sources. Lineage and
refresh detail stays in the log file. Reference: docs/reference/mcp-tools.md.

tools.description:
Pull the official line into a live worktree. Returns synced,
already-current, would-sync, sync-active, sync-resolution-required,
memory-sync-choice-required or blocked, with next-call arguments and a log path.
Tree changes mark the prior review pre-sync and offer a new review; sync movement
never blocks. The product merges memory lines only here; raw git merge is a hand edit
it cannot prevent. Every memory landing judges its tree; a fast-forward judges what
it adopts before moving any ref.

Reference: docs/reference/mcp-tools.md.
tools.name: worktree_sync

tools.description: PAUSE an atomic master: it stops, hands control back, and releases the master's atomic-series activation selection. Publishes NOTHING: publication is a separate, explicitly requested PUBLICATION through worktree_checkpoint_landing. States: paused, blocked. Answers the state reached and the next call. Reference: docs/reference/mcp-tools.md.
tools.name: worktree_pause

tools.description:
Land one verified series code commit with its memory content through a durable direct-
landing generation, recovering through worktree_operation_control. States: landed,
would-land, refused. Answers the state, what blocks and the next call; the whole result
is in the log file. Reference: docs/reference/mcp-tools.md.

tools.description:
Give, take back, or reclaim direct-execution grants, as an architect.

A leaf runs directly on its master's branch only while a grant for
it exists, and only a caller bound to the architect role may call
this. ``action`` is ``give``, ``revoke`` or ``reclaim``; giving a
grant that exists, or taking back one that does not, changes nothing
and says so. Reclaim takes back one task's grants that no leaf still
requires. The grant is read at the moment of every call.
MUTATING (grant record only).
Reference: docs/reference/mcp-tools.md.

Preview a worktree closeout without mutating: the count of changed code paths and
proposed commits with subjects up to the list bound, and what blocks (states:
would-closeout, blocked, closeout-gate-blocked). A preview is a read; the whole result
is in the log file.
Reference: docs/reference/mcp-tools.md.
tools.name: worktree_closeout_preview

tools.description:
Apply an approved worktree closeout and return promptly. States: closed, blocked,
closeout-gate-blocked. Answers the state reached and the next call; the whole result
is in the log file. Delivered-against-reviewed names
same, different, or no review recorded. Poll worktree_status for progress.
Reference: docs/reference/mcp-tools.md.

tools.description:
Archive lifecycle evidence, then remove worktrees, merged branches, reports, logs and
the enclosure root once integrated. States: cleanup-completed, already-clean, would-cleanup,
blocked, provider-setup-running. Answers the state reached; a dry run with
blockers answers a blocked state. Reference: docs/reference/mcp-tools.md.
tools.name: worktree_cleanup

tools.description:
Abandon a worktree task without integrating, preserving terminal archive proof. States: abandoned, would-abandon, abandon-blocked, blocked. Answers the state reached
and the next call. Reference: docs/reference/mcp-tools.md.
tools.name: worktree_abandon

tools.description:
Reopen a COMPLETED leaf under its exact same leaf id: review, closeout and integration
state returns to virgin and the leaf document goes back to planning. A cleaned-up leaf
behind its master's tip restarts from that tip when its recorded landing is an ancestor
of it; a landing not on the line refuses. Afterwards edit
steps via task_doc, then run a normal worktree_start. States: reopened, blocked;
preview with dry_run. Reference: docs/reference/mcp-tools.md.
tools.name: task_reopen

tools.description:
Prove the landed edge and complete one parent-child task lifecycle edge: refuses before
cleanup unless every declared step is done, then reconciles the exact parent row.
Leaves require a master; ancestors are not completed. States: finalized,
would-finalize, blocked. Answers the state, what blocks
and the next call; preview with dry_run. Reference: docs/reference/mcp-tools.md.
tools.name: lifecycle_finalize_task

tools.description: Write task documents: ar-task-document/v1 JSON and generated markdown. Read the .md as a file. A write names its kind ['subTask'|'master']. Operations: create, replace, set_status, set_step, add_step, remove_step, skip_step, set_subtask, remove_subtask, set_section, append_decision, put_open_question, begin_review, record_review, record_route_review, author_execution_graph, attach_master, detach_master, retire_master, archive_sprint, linkage_report, set_field. Writes answer ok; dry runs answer wouldLose and the diff. Reference: docs/reference/mcp-tools.md.
tools.name: task_doc

tools.description: Prepare, publish, inspect or validate one leaf's curator-coherence authority. Publish requires semantic_requirement_revision, delivery_attempt, expected_predecessor_digest, expected_code_candidate_tree, expected_memory_candidate_tree, expected_task_topology_fingerprint, expected_task_intent, expected_attestation_sha256 and caller; supply judgments or judgments_file. The stable manifest is authoritative, never Markdown. Longer explanation: docs/tool-details.md.

tools.description: Start one role agent for one canonical selection with the caller as parent, starting in Paseo. Only a role agent that AR launched can call this. A request id reconciles the same agent, never a second. Only the agent that started an execution repeats its request_id. Answers ok, the agent id and the handover location; rejected (the launch is closed; no usable agent exists). Starts run one at a time. A call waits up to 60 seconds for another start to end, then is refused; nextAction says to call again with the same arguments. Reference: docs/reference/mcp-tools.md.

tools.description: Start a leaf's Worker, Reviewer and Curator in one call (MIK-R100 rule 1). Only a role agent that AR launched can call this. Only the leaf's owning Manager may call it. Pass selection, request_id and per-seat launch choices. Worker opens; Reviewer and Curator are held unless reviewer_message opens the Reviewer. A repeat with the same request id reconciles the same three agents: it creates no fourth and opens no held seat. More: docs/tool-details.md.

tools.name: role_start_set

tools.description: Send one text message to one role agent. Name the recipient by agent_id or by role plus task references. Only the host request is promised: without wait the call answers once the host accepted the message; with wait it answers when the consuming turn ends (finished, failed, cancelled, permission, timeout). A mid-turn recipient gets the message in its turn, which the host may cancel; a waiting, unstarted or unwritable recipient is answered `held` with reason, permission, counts and id. Only a full hold store (twenty) is refused as `recipient-busy`. Reference: docs/reference/mcp-tools.md.

tools.name: role_message

tools.description:
Name records of one memory-tree view.

Views: source_context, invariant, family, record, weakness (open by file, kind or sentence),
dependent (documents and their links). `recordId` takes a text ID (`INV-…`, `WKN-…`, `DPD-…`).
Rows name ID, kind, state and location, never text. Filters: `sourcePath`, `weaknessKind`,
`includeClosed`, `staleOnly`, `standsOn`. `repositoryRoot` and `codeTreeId` select the measured
code tree. Writes: `agents-remember knowledge-ingest` or `agents-remember knowledge-bootstrap`.
Docs: docs/reference/mcp-tools.md.
tools.name: knowledge_read

tools.description:
Name the changed records of two memory trees beside a report (MIK-R109).

The whole comparison is a caller-readable report: every changed file
with its patch, grouped by record and source path. The answer holds
the two trees, the counts by kind, the changed records, and the
report's location. With no `afterRevision`, HEAD meets the working
tree, which writes loose, unreferenced objects. Narrow with
`recordId`/`path`; absent selectors refused, unconverted sides as
`legacy-format`. Longer explanation: docs/reference/mcp-tools.md.
tools.name: knowledge_diff

tools.description:
Run the knowledge validator (MIK-R22) over one converted memory tree and return its
report: `validation.ok`, the refusal and report-only counts, the counts by rule, and the
first violations (refusing ones first; `violationsTruncated` says when more exist). Name a
leaf by `contractPath`: the validator reads the leaf's memory worktree against its
recorded memory base and its code worktree, and the response adds the leaf's latest
change-to-knowledge worklist (MIK-R08): its state, digest, item counts and items, with the
persisted file's path for every item's facts. Or name a tree directly with `memoryRoot`
and its paired code checkout `codeRoot`. `baseCommits` are memory commits to compare
anchors with; with none, every anchor is checked for path existence. An unconverted tree
or a database file is refused as `legacy-format`. The tool reads only: it writes no file
and opens no database.
tools.name: knowledge_integrity_check

tools.description:
Plan or commit one knowledge write (MIK-R73 rule 1).

`contractPath` names a leaf, or with `crossing` a master's open crossing sync; the
contract guards the write and names the only memory worktree it may write. `repoId`
with `wave` writes a taskless wave. Give the hand-off as `handoff` with
`handoffName`, or as `handoffPath`. Without `commit` (the default) it plans,
validates and writes nothing; with it, it writes files and commits nothing to Git. A
refusal lists every problem, and the whole report is a file the answer names. Longer
explanation: docs/reference/mcp-tools.md.
tools.name: knowledge_write

tools.description:
Update or retire one leaf's explainer, or claim a master as its architect. `action` is
`update`, `retire` or `claim`; `leaf_id` names the leaf for the two leaf actions, and a
`retire` carries its `receipt_id`. `claim` is open to any hosted architect seat, writes the
master-to-architect record and moves that master's held reports to the claiming seat.
`update` and `retire` are accepted only from the seat that record names; any other caller
is refused `not-this-masters-architect` and claims first.
Reference: docs/reference/mcp-tools.md.
tools.name: explainer_control
